limits: Attachment counting: the six attachments are identical in assignment-1 and assignment-2 packets apart from the source-URL line (verified by diff); each is counted once. Prompts and rubric fields are counted per assignment; assignment-2's copy of the prior assignment-1 prompt contains no citations.

All text read is the repository's extraction of the pinned upstream files (no OCR). No attachment page was marked as lacking extracted text. The 303-page 2023 Annual Report is mostly numeric tables; 16 near-empty pages are section dividers or charts with little text, and chart/table layouts in the extraction scramble some row/column labels (affects one motion citation marked UNABLE_TO_VERIFY).
The Davis Complaint is a DOCX conversion; original pagination is not retained, so complaint locations are by paragraph.
The Langenhorst attachment runs from the majority's 'Affirmed.' directly into Justice Garman's dissent (PDF pp.12-20) without a dissent heading; dissent locations are labelled in this file.

Counting unit: each citation string (full cite, short form with reporter or pin cite, statute/rule/regulation section, or quoted/named authority in the prompt or rubric) in each unique matter document; parallel reporter cites in one string count once. Bare case-name references with no reporter or pin cite inside the three supplied opinions (e.g. 'In Dawdy, ...') are not separately counted. Repeated identical table-header rule labels on one Annual Report page are counted once per page. Citations in the motion and rubric to the scenario's own record (complaint paragraphs, affidavits, exhibits) are record references, not legal authority, and are not counted; the scenario case caption is recorded as fictional.

Pin-cite checks for Illinois Reports pages rely on page markers in CourtListener's Harvard CAP text (mapped with a constant per-opinion offset confirmed against several known pins); where no markers were available the proposition, not the page, was checked.

Statutes and Supreme Court Rules were read in their current official versions (ILGA, illinoiscourts.gov compiled rules current to Oct. 16, 2026). Historical editions cited in the opinions (e.g. West 1992/2000, 134 Ill. 2d Rules) were not read; where numbering changed (Rule 306) this is flagged.
The 2023 Annual Report attachment was checked only against itself (it is the cited document); it was not compared with the AOIC's published PDF.

The assignment-1 prompt contains an uncited legal assertion (venue in wrongful death proper where any part of the action occurred, including the place of death); with no authority named or quoted it is not counted. The assignment-2 prompt's sentence is counted because it quotes Langenhorst's language verbatim.
Embedded pin cites to Dawdy (76) and Guerine (44) inside Langenhorst were checked by reading those opinions with Illinois Reports page markers; each record carries a page-specific excerpt.

Not read: Restatement (Second) of Conflict of Laws § 84 cmt. c; the Maag, Kitch and Sunderland law-review articles; the 2000 AOIC Annual Report; the text of the Guerine appendix supervisory orders; the Rules of Professional Conduct, Rules of Evidence and Code of Judicial Conduct amendment histories. These citations are UNABLE_TO_VERIFY, not problems.

Embedded citations in the three supplied opinions were checked for identity via CourtListener citation lookup and, for propositions, by reading the cited passage on CourtListener; supplied opinion texts were themselves compared with CourtListener's official text at sampled passages (matching).

No upstream scripts were run, and no paid APIs were used. CourtListener was reached through its connector. ILGA pages were fetched directly; the site's TLS chain needed the published Sectigo intermediate certificate, and verification was not disabled.

The original exclusion of bare case-name references was corrected by a complete supplemental scan of readable text. It adds 97 named-authority short forms, all checked against judicial text; the first second-review worker's eleven additions are included exactly once. Primary-source access and extraction limits remain as stated.

citations.location: assignment-2 criterion_6 (required, +3 pts), "criterion" field
citations.authority: Langenhorst v. Norfolk Southern Ry. Co., 219 Ill. 2d 430, 848 N.E.2d 927 (2006)
citations.citation_as_written: Langenhorst v. Norfolk S. Ry. Co. 219 Ill. 2d 430 (Ill. 2006)
citations.cited_for: Affidavit of Liam Vance that DuPage would be inconvenient, "as required under Langenhorst"
citations.context: Identifies in Assignment #2 that the affidavit by Liam Vance indicates that DuPage County would be an inconvenient forum for him to litigate this case as required under Langenhorst v. Norfolk S. Ry. Co. 219 Ill. 2d 430 (Ill. 2006).

first_check.explanation: Langenhorst (attachment pp.3, 7, 10) places the burden on the defendant to show that the plaintiff's chosen forum is inconvenient to the defendant and that another forum is more convenient to all parties; it observes that no affidavits said the CHOSEN forum (St. Clair) was inconvenient. It contains no requirement that a plaintiff or plaintiff's witnesses file affidavits that the TRANSFEREE forum would be inconvenient. The criterion's 'as required under Langenhorst' therefore attributes to Langenhorst a requirement it does not state. Such affidavits may be strategically useful (they rebut the 'more convenient to all parties' prong), so a second check should weigh whether 'as required' can fairly be read as 'as relevant under'.
first_check.excerpt_read: Supplied Langenhorst opinion PDF p.10: 'In this case, no affidavits have been filed stating that St. Clair County would be an inconvenient forum for any of the witnesses. ... We reiterate that the defendant must show that the plaintiff's chosen forum is inconvenient to the defendant and that another forum is more convenient to all parties.'

second_check.explanation: Assignment-2 criterion_6 turns a useful rebuttal affidavit into something 'required under Langenhorst.' At PDF p.10 the majority discusses missing affidavits about inconvenience in the plaintiff's chosen St. Clair forum and puts the transfer burden on defendants. It does not require physician or plaintiff affidavits proving inconvenience in the proposed DuPage forum. The criterion's literal legal attribution is overstated, although the affidavit could be relevant evidence.
second_check.excerpt_read: Langenhorst attachment PDF pp.7,10: defendants must prove the chosen forum inconvenient and another more convenient to all; p.10 discusses absent affidavits about St. Clair, the chosen forum.

first_check.explanation: Inverts Guerine's holding. Guerine p.8 holds that a trial court ABUSES ITS DISCRETION IN GRANTING transfer where the witnesses are scattered among several counties including the chosen forum and no county predominates; the motion says Guerine held transfer is 'warranted only where' those conditions exist. The quoted words are accurate; the framing reverses their meaning. (The motion's next sentences use the holding correctly, so the error may be a drafting slip, but as written it misstates the holding.)
first_check.excerpt_read: Supplied Guerine opinion PDF p.8: 'we hold that a trial court abuses its discretion in granting an intrastate forum non conveniens motion to transfer venue where, as here, the potential trial witnesses are scattered among several counties, including the plaintiff's chosen forum, and no single county enjoys a predominant connection to the litigation.'

second_check.explanation: The defense motion quotes Guerine's witness pattern accurately but introduces it as a condition where transfer is 'warranted only.' Guerine's holding is the inverse: granting transfer on that pattern is an abuse of discretion. The motion's later application points in the right direction, suggesting a drafting slip, but it does not cure the sentence as written. First American/First National caption variation is not a defect.
second_check.excerpt_read: Guerine attachment PDF p.8: court holds transfer on the scattered-witness/no-predominant-county pattern is an abuse of discretion; motion PDF p.5 calls transfer on that pattern warranted.
